title: MV/MZ RPG Maker Cook Tool Deluxe [R6.04u7]

posts.author: AceOfAces
posts.body:
English and Greek translations are included.
The RPG Maker Cook Tool Deluxe is the successor of the
original tool
. Rebuilt from the ground up, brings a ton of publishing features (on top of the robust compiler and packer tool) in a speedy, smaller package.
Features
Spoiler
Great experience for all: Utilizing Nw.js' JavaScript source protection, the games' source code is protected without sacrificing the developer's or the user's experience with the game. It's far more compatible than tools like Enigma VirtualBox and doesn't sacrifice performance.
Faster and better than ever: with a mix of a new UI framework and .NET NativeAOT technology, the tool is faster and uses far less memory and space.
An arsenal of tools for a perfect build: In addition to compiling and packing, new tools have been added so you can make a custom build. No need of extra tools. These are:
Hotpatch: No more manual patching of JS files! The compiler will now patch the files for you.
Asset Protection: Ensures that the assets aren't easily accessible. Using a plugin that compresses and/or encrypts the database? It takes care of any possible issues, too.
Nw.js Manager: Easily download the latest (or a specific) version of Nw.js you need, whenever you need newer features or shipping on platforms like Steam. It even prepares the final binary with a new icon and the details you input.
Metadata Editor: By exposing relevant settings for Nw.js apps, the editor allows you to fine-tune the behavior of the game's executable.
Asset Compressor: Combining the popular WebP and Opus Compression Tools, Asset Compressor compresses the files to WebP and Opus, with minimal to no quality loss.
[R5.01+] Font Compressor: Utilizes woff2 compression for fonts, reducing the size of the game and speeding up loading times.
Streamlined work flow: It's as easy as finding the exported game, pick the engine version and click build. You can even utilize the recipe files to quickly ready the compiler.

posts.author: AceOfAces
posts.body: Released a hotfix for the tool (R5.01 Update 3). This addresses the issue where setting the version of NW.js to "Auto-Detect" will always pick the version that is suitable for RPG Maker MV games, even if the game was made with RPG Maker MZ. It also updates to the final version of Avalonia 11.0.5, which brings additional bug and security fixes (specifically, a security fix for Skia).

posts.author: AceOfAces
posts.body:
Released R5.02 today. The latest update on the RPG Maker Cook Tool Deluxe (codenamed “Kestrel”) brings a number of improvements, alongside changes for the upcoming Halva Bootstrapper v2.
Changelog:
Spoiler
Overhauled project management:
Overhauled the recipe file architecture for easier expandability. (Recipe files created by older versions are not compatible. Migration tool is coming a little later.)
You can now set defaults for new projects.
Added the option to create new recipe on the “Project and Utilities” menu.
Improved the algorithm for determining the engine version.
Improvements to the Halva packaging system:
Expanded the settings for the upcoming Halva Bootstrapper v2.
If the Halva compression type is selected, the Cook Tool will put the NW.js files to the “Binaries” folder in the project’s output.
Improved the logging system.
UI improvements:
Moved the utilities to the “Utilities” sub-menu.
Added tooltips to most of the settings in the Project Settings menu.
Fixed some typos.
Fixed an error, where the version numbers were mixed up.
Fixed a bug where the “Use the computer’s RAM for compression” option didn’t apply properly.

Changelog:
Spoiler

posts.author: AceOfAces
posts.body:
R5.02 Update 2 was released today! Alongside a few fixes, it also includes a copy of the Halva Bootstrapper (v2.0). The new Halva Bootstrapper is much more straightforward, and it's easier to customize. All that the player has to do is to simply run the "Dragonhouse.GameBootstrapper" executable. A minor thing, it is recommended to reset your default settings before using this (and adjust the folder settings for Halva for existing recipe files), as it can cause a mess if not fixed.
If you are wondering about Halva: it's a far more efficient archive format than Zip. Alongside better resilience against cracking, it's also more efficient for pushing out patches.
Changelog:
Includes a copy of the Halva Bootstrapper 2.0.
The Cook Tool will now copy the required files to the game's output.
Adjusted the default settings so it avoids potential issues with the Halva Bootstrapper.
Performance and stability improvements.
Fixed an error where the question for resetting the default settings only showed an OK button.

posts.author: AceOfAces
posts.body:
With 2023 almost ending, a new update for RPG Maker Cook Tool Deluxe has arrived! R5.03 (codenamed "Kestrel 2"), brings data validation. This is used to verify that the settings are set up properly. This prevents potential issues that could occur from user error. I've also re-enabled the advanced settings that reside in the Metadata Editor. Previously, leaving these empty would cause an error that neither the nodejs main and background scripts could be found. This version will simply mark them as null when they are empty instead.
Changelog:
Spoiler
Implemented data validation.
Prevents user error in areas where this could cause issues for the game.
For the compiler, it will show a message that the package.json file isn't present, and point them to the Metadata Editor.
Restored the options to set the Nodejs main and background scripts.
If these settings are empty, they will be set to null in the package.json file, fixing the issue where the game wouldn't load due to missing main/background script.
Fixed an issue, where the converter settings were mixed up. The "Use WebP" would disable the "Use Opus" setting and vice versa.
Fixed an issue with the converters, where pressing the Cancel button for the first time would carry over the cancel request to the subsequent tasks.
Fixed a typo in the logs. When the converter would search for audio files, the log would claim that it's searching for images, not audio.
Have a wonderful new year!

posts.author: AceOfAces
posts.body:
Well... Talk about rapid fire fixes.
Cook Tool Deluxe has been updated twice. The first time, it fixes issues with the Halva Bootstrapper. The second is to fix an issue with data validation false flagging the windows icon setting.
For the first update: due to a typo in the relative cache folder location, the game wouldn't launch properly. The typo has been fixed, but two actions are required for existing users of the tool:
Reset your default settings. This is necessary, so the issue doesn't persist.
For any recipe files that were created before this version, you will need to edit the settings and fix the error. If it's not fixed, the editor will not let you save. To fix this:
Turn on "Compress files" (if you have it turned on.
On the Compiler and packer settings, set the compression type to Halva.
Open the Halva settings and fix the relative cache folder location (remove the first '/').
Roll back the changes in steps 1 and 2. Then save.
For the second update, it's a slight re-tool of how it validated the path. Previously, it checked for invalid characters for file names. This caused the issue of showing an error for invalid characters. R5.03 Update 2 changes the list of invalid characters to the one for the path. It essentially checks if the path has invalid characters.
Changelog:
R5.03 Update 1
Spoiler
Fixed a typo that broke the path constructor for the bootstrapper. This would result in the game not booting.
Changed the default version of NW.js to 0.48.4. Fixes an issue where the game wouldn't boot.
Added data validation for the relative cache location.
Fixed a minor typo in the game master.
R5.03 Update 2
Spoiler
Fixed the validation for the Windows Icon setting. It would show a message that there are invalid characters in the path, even if the user used the Browse button or was written properly.

posts.author: AceOfAces
posts.body:
Happy new year, maties!
This update fixes some issues regarding data validation. It also includes a change that was meant for a future release: Packaging as a zip file is removed, in favor of Halva (which has better asset protection and it's far more efficient). Games compiled with this version onwards will pack the files with Halva (which is far better in asset protection and provides better compression). The game simply launches from the provided "Dragonhouse.GameBootstrapper" executable.
Changelog:
Updated .NET to version 8.0.1. Brings minor stability improvements and security fixes.
Removed the option to pack the files into Zip (Halva does a far better job, anyway).
Improved the logging system.
Fixed an issue where the Metadata Editor wasn't available.
Fixed an issue where creating a package.json file for games didn't unlock the build option.
Fixed an issue where certain settings would show a message (when they are not required). This affected the Metadata editor.

posts.author: AceOfAces
posts.body:
With the release of version 1.8.0 of RPG Maker MZ, a new version of Cook Tool Deluxe has arrived! This update brings these key changes:
It's now compatible with RPG Maker MZ 1.8.0.
The bootstrapper can be customized now. You can change the executable's information and icon.
Custom files and folders can be added to the packages now. Originally, the code assumed that the game only had the standard folders. With this update, you can add additional files to the packages.
There are more changes (including a vastly improved recipe migration system), which make the tool even better.
Changelog:
Fixed compatibility issues with RPG Maker MZ 1.8.0.
You can now add custom files and folders to Halva packages.
Dragonbones is added by default in the database package.
This is only required for additional files that aren’t part of a standard RPG Maker project (such as the aforementioned Dragonbones folder, if it’s stored on the root folder of the project).
The bootstrapper can be customized.
If the default JSON files cannot be loaded, it will record the error in the log.
Implemented code that updates the default settings and recipe files (to improve compatibility).
This was partially implemented since R5.02, but this update makes it far more robust.
Updated Avalonia to 11.0.7. Brings performance and stability improvements.

posts.author: AceOfAces
posts.body:
Released R5.04 Update 1 today! This adds AV1 Image Format (AVIF) to the Asset compressor. This gives better compression ration (compared to lossy WebP). There are a few bug fixes as well.
Changelog:
AV1 Image Format (AVIF) has been added to the converter!
AVIF brings a better compression ratio compared to lossy WebP.
Asset Compressor now skips the git files.
Fixed a bug, where hitting the Cancel button on the converter (during conversion) wouldn't stop the conversion.
Fixed a bug where the data validation for the bootstrapper's icon didn't trigger.

posts.author: AceOfAces
posts.body:
Released R5.04 Update 2 today! This update expands on the customization of the bootstrapper, alongside fixing some issues. The customizations are for adding a splash image and add the option to save into the base folder (requires the free plugin in the downloads page). Adding a custom splash image to the bootstrapper can add a bit of spice (or build a bit of intrigue).
A thing to note: The bootstrapper is theme-aware. Depending on the user's settings, it will switch between dark and light themes. This may affect the readability of the text. Make sure that the image doesn't affect this. Using a gradient or transparency (in the bottom part of the image) can help with this.
Changelog:​
Added the option to show a splash image for the bootstrapper.
The icon of the bootstrapper window should be using the correct one.
Added the option to set a title for the bootstrapper window.
Added the option to change the save location to the base folder (requires the FSDK_AdvSaveHandler plugin).
The location is related to the bootstrapper.
This is only necessary for games that save on the game's folder.
Removed the option to change the bootstrapper internal name (Bootstrapper Name), in order to avoid compatibility issues.
Improved the cleanup routine.
If the recipe file is made with a newer version of the Cook Tool, it will skip loading it. This is necessary, as newer versions could use a newer format of the recipe file.
Fixed a bug in the bootstrapper, where the app would hang (or otherwise crash) when an error occurred.
Updated Avalonia to 11.0.8. Brings stability improvements and miscellaneous bug fixes.

posts.author: AceOfAces
posts.body:
Released R5.05 today! This update is a behind-the-scenes re-work, which streamlines the tool and brings a few quality of life improvements.
Changelog:
Merged the Bootstrapper Settings and Executable Metadata tab into the "Customization" tab.
This is enabled when the option to change the exe metadata is turned on.
Improvements to the Halva Bootstrapper:
Re-worked the structure of the manifest.
Added manifest version and file integrity checks.
The Game Master executable is now stored to the Binaries folder.
Improved package version checks.
Improvements to the Asset Compressor:
Implemented a bit of code to improve the copying of the audio's metadata.
Fixed an error, where AVIF Chroma Subsampling was set to 4:2:0, instead of 4:2:2. Chrome subsampling 4:2:0 would result in images being greyscale.
Updated .NET to 8.0.2. Brings stability improvements.
Slipstreamed the latest patches for ImageMagick. Brings stability improvements.

posts.author: AceOfAces
posts.body:
Released R5.05 Update 2 today! This update fixes some critical bugs.
The SDK version of the NW.js is only downloaded if the option to compile the JavaScript code is turned on.
Fixed a bug with the migration code. If the original recipe file (or default settings file) has the setting for the cache location empty, it would cause the loading mechanism to break. This bug would break the tool.
[R5.05u1] Fixed an issue where setting a different executable name for the game would cause the bootstrapper to show a message that some files were missing.
R5.05 Update 1 was released a few days ago to fix the above critical issue. Updating to the latest version includes that.

posts.author: AceOfAces
posts.body:
Released R5.06 today! This update (codenamed Sparrow) brings various quality of life improvements, alongside some technical improvements.
Re-worked the mechanism for downloading the relevant NW.js files.
Improves the memory usage when downloading these files.
This may improve build times as well.
Added a screen that allows the immediate addition of additional files to the packages.
It will show up when you either select the project’s location by clicking on the Browse button or clicking on Import in the project settings.
[Game Bootstrapper] Added support for cases where the game is packaged into an MSIX package (such as builds for the Microsoft Store).
Moved the “Product Version” into the common settings.
The manifest that is create will also reference that.
This is reserved for a future feature.
Fixed a bug, where clicking on “Download selected version” would skip the download of the binaries for NW.js (but it would download the SDK version of NW.js).
Slipstreamed patches for ImageMagick. Improves stability.
Updated cwebp (used for WebP compression). Brings performance and stability improvements.
[Plugin] Fixed an error, where the path to the save files on Linux/Mac were on a different place than expected.

posts.author: AceOfAces
posts.body:
Released R5.06 Update 1 today! This adds AV1 video compression to the asset compressor and brings stability and performance improvements.
Changelog:
Added AV1 Video Compression to the asset compression.
Brings improved compression vs VP8/VP9.
This is turned off by default, as it requires a powerful CPU or a system with hardware acceleration to play the videos.
Fixed a bug, where using AVIF compression could throw an error, breaking the image compression.
Fixed a bug, where cancelling the task and then restart, it would mangle the path. This would throw an error where the path doesn't exist.
Updated ImageMagick to 7.1.1-31. Brings improved performance and stability.
Windows specific changes:
Updated rcedit to 2.0.0. Brings bug fixes.
Updated ffmpeg to 7.0. Brings performance improvements.
Fixed an issue, where the tool and the included bootstrapper would crash, if the system didn't support the SSE4.2 instruction set.

posts.author: AceOfAces
posts.body:
Released R5.06 Update 2 today!
This update provides additional security improvements and some quality of life improvements (particularly if you use an installer for the game or you published it on Steam).
Important: A plugin must be installed, in order to take full advantage of the security features that this update includes. Have it turned off while you are working on the game via the editor and then turn it on when exporting.  If your game is compatible, it’s also recommended to enable the “Compile source files” option in the project settings.
Changelog:
Added the option to put the final build to a sub-folder.
Added additional security measures for games that are packed with Halva.
If available, the bootstrapper will use WebP images for the splash screen.
If the WebP converter isn’t removed, it will convert the selected image to lossless WebP image.
Added the following command line arguments for the bootstrapper (useful for projects where they opt into not reseting the cache after the game closes.
These are useful for cases where either an installer or Steam is involved.
The following arguments are as follows:
–rebuild: Rebuilds the cache.
–cleanup: Clears the cache.
–prebuild: Builds the cache on demand.
Compatibility improvements for the Game Master component.

posts.author: AceOfAces
posts.body:
Released R5.06 Update 3 today! This update is focused on improving the performance and reliability of the bootstrapper, alongside updating some dependencies.
IMPORTANT: If you have the game set up to keep the cache (even when the game closes), an error about corrupt cache will appear. This is due to the new integrity checks using different values for verifying the cache files (thus, it's false positive). Once the cache is re-created, it will load the correct values. If you left the default setting for the cache (which is to reset the cache when the game closes), this does not affect you.
Changelog:
Overhauled the file integrity checks.
Substantially improves launch times for the bootstrapper.
Updated .NET to 8.0.5. Brings stability and security improvements.
Updated ImageMagick to 7.1.1-32. Brings stability improvements.
[Linux] Updated FFmpeg to 7.0. Brings performance improvements.
Updated SkiaSharp to 2.88.8. Brings stability improvements.
Fixed a bug in the bootstrapper, where an error about wrong parameters.
Fixed a bug in the bootstrapper, where rebuilding the cache would result in re-doing the extraction step on the next launch.

posts.author: AceOfAces
posts.body:
Released R5.06 Update 4 today! This is a minor update that rolls up some fixes regarding Halva compression and update some dependencies.
Changelog:
Improvements to the stability and speed of Halva Package System.
Updated dependencies:
Updated to .NET 8.0.6 (8.0.5 in Linux). Brings stability and security improvements.
Slipstreamed updates to ImageMagick, improving stability.
[Windows] Updated FFmpeg to 7.0.1. Brings stability improvements.
Updated Serilog to 4.0.0. Brings stability improvements in log related actions.
[Plugin Pack – Cook Tool Add-On] Fixed a typo in the plugin that prevented the game from starting up.
[Plugin Pack – Cook Tool Add-On] Re-factored the code to improve the reliability of the plugin.

posts.author: AceOfAces
posts.body:
Released R5.06 Update 5 today! This is a hotfix that addresses some issues with the strict cache integrity checks option (introduced as part of R5.06u2), alongisde the option to turn it on/off.
Changelog:
Added the option to enable/disable the strict cache integrity checks (introduced in R5.06 Update 2).
This is primarily used for prevented cheats and malware via tampering the files.
This option can be toggled when the setting to delete the cache every time the game closes.
Fixed some errors in the Greek translation.
Fixed a bug caused by a race condition. This would prevent the creation of the file catalog (required for the strict cache integrity checks).
While you are here: As I am planning out the next updates for the tool, I'll need your input. I would like to know how the tool works for you, what features you'd like to see (both for you and your players) and what to improve. If you have some time to spare, please fill out the survey:
https://forms.office.com/r/pue3EiCPzd
Your feedback is highly appreciated.

posts.author: AceOfAces
posts.body:
Released R5.07 today! This update (codenamed Sparrow 2) is focussing on streamlining the build process and be more flexible (useful for future features down the pipeline).
Added the option to generate a manifest for the itch.io app.
This tells the app which executable to launch, alongside installing the latest version of DirectX.
This also addresses the issue for games that don't use compression, where the app asks which executable to launch.
If the package.json file is missing the required details, a window to fill them in will show up.
Re-tooled the Halva's package management to be more flexible.
Slightly re-tooled the file catalog loading mechanism.
The option for the strict cache checking is opt-in now.
Fixed an error, where the "Verifying cache..." text is shown on the bootstrap window briefly, when it's not necessary.

posts.author: AceOfAces
posts.body:
Released R5.07 Update 1 today! This update brings fixes for the bootstrapper, alongside an update to dependencies.
Changelog:
Updated Avalonia to 11.1.0-rc.2, improving stability.
Fixed a bug, where the version checking was between the game config file with itself. This would result into not updating the cache (if the developer opted into not clearing the cache after the game closes).
Fixed a bug with strict cache integrity check. Due to the game master not terminating the file watcher, it would crash when it tried to clear the cache.

posts.author: AceOfAces
posts.body:
Released R5.07 Update 2 today! This update is (primarily) a rollup of updates for the tool's dependencies, alongside a few quality-of-life improvements.
Performance improvements.
[Linux] Enabled Vulkan support for rendering the UI (if available).
[Windows] Enabled support for Windows.UI.Composition (falls back to DirectComposition if not). Improves support for high refresh rates.
Updated the following dependencies:
Updated .NET to 8.0.7. Brings stability and security improvements.
Updated Avalonia to 11.1.0. Brings additional performance and stability improvements.
Rolled up the latest updates for ImageMagick. Brings stability improvements.
Adjusted the filters so it doesn't copy the Mapshots folder to the final output.

posts.author: AceOfAces
posts.body:
Released R5.08 today!
This update (codenamed Soufflé) brings quality of life improvements. There’s also a slightly experimental build of the Game Master for Steam (primarily so it can work with Steam Proton on Linux).
Changelog:
Moved the utilities into their own section in the menu.
Introduced a bit of code to not allow the bootstrapper to launch again (if the game is launched already).
NW.js is always single instance, anyway.
Updated dependencies, improving performance and stability.
Tweaked some of the text, improving clarity.
Improved the accuracy of the filter used in certain file copy procedures.
This is primarily to strip out files from NW.js, if you export the game as a desktop game.
It’s recommended to always export as a web browser build, to ensure a clean build. The tool will convert it into a desktop game automatically.
Fixed an error in the metadata editor. Browsing for the icon would change the location of the html file instead.

posts.author: AceOfAces
posts.body:
Released R5.09 today! This update (codenamed "Sous Vide") brings a batch of quality-of-life improvements, support for MZ v1.8.1 and integrating the Steam Proton support files to the tool.
Changelog:
Updated to .NET 9 (RC1), bringing performance and size improvements.
Now compatible with RPG maker MZ 1.8.1.
Added (initial) Steam support.
[Windows] The Steam Proton files are now integrated to the main bundle for the bootstrap.
[Windows] You now have the option to create a separate, Steam Proton compatible build.
Greenworks.js is now added to the custom files and folders (applies if Greenworks must be in the game’s parent folder).
Files for the lib folder are now added to the Halva packages by default.
It will also strip out library files that don’t apply for the OS that the game is built on.
This is primarily for supporting Steam, but it could support for other libraries as well.
Added the option to create a test build.
This will use the SDK version of NW.js. This allows access to the Dev Tools (useful for diagnosing issues that could happen after building the final build).
Fixed a bug, where the bootstrapper would hang on the “Checking game files” stage, if the game was in a folder that doesn’t allow write access.
Minor fit and finish updates.

posts.author: AceOfAces
posts.body:
Released R5.10 today! This update (codenamed "Sous Vide Grande") contains a small, but substantial update: the upgrade to Halva 2. The new, overhauled version of Halva brings performance and security improvements. Specifically, there are under the hood changes that improve compression and decompression performance, alongside improving security. Although it sounds like an update to the existing Halva system, the under the hood and file changes create new files. Hence, why this update has the R5.10 version.
If you are using a service like Steam to distribute your game, the patches to your users will end up bigger than anticipated. This is normal, as the packages are different despite carrying the same files. Updates that your release after that first build with this version should come back to normal.
Changelog:
Updated Halva Package System to v2.
Overhauled internals and file architecture to improve performance and security.
Packages will carry the .halva2 file extension.
Updated dependencies and .NET, bringing performance and stability improvements.
The name used by the bootstrapper will now use the "Product Name" text in the project settings.
Tweaked the Customization tab. If the option to compress the game files is turned on, the access to the options for the Splash screen and icon should available now.

posts.author: AceOfAces
posts.body:
After some feedback and assisting with getting a game to work with it, I can confidently say that the tool can create Steam Deck compatible builds. There was quite the guesswork to get stuff working (primarily with Steam Input. The Steamworks documentation didn't do a good explanation on how it latches on to the game), but recent updates have improved on that front. And looking on said feedback, I covered the bases for supporting Steam Deck out of the box. This update will change one more default setting to make it easier to bring over your game to the Deck (specifically, building a Steam Proton/WINE compatible build). This won't be applied if you are updating from an older patch, but you can edit the default settings via the tool.
Alongside this update, I'm adding experimental support for hardware encoding videos to AV1. This requires very recent hardware (AMD Radeon RX700/GeForce RTX 30/Intel Arc series and newer), but it will speed up the encoding. It's experimental, as I do need to do more work on it (including automating the selection of the appropriate encoder for your graphics card). If you are feeling a bit adventurous, feel free to test it out and give me some feedback.
Changelog:
Added Hardware Encoding support for converting videos to AV1.
In Windows, selecting the Hardware Encoder will use the GPU manufacturer's API (Quick Sync Video, NVENC, AMD VCE).
On Linux, Intel and AMD cards will use Video Acceleration API (usually used with Mesa drivers. Your distro may be using these drivers already).
This is a work in progress and there may be issues. If you don't want to deal with that, leave the option to Software.
Adjusted the default option for "Create a Steam Proton/WINE compatible build" to ON.

posts.body:
NinefoldSpirit said:
packages everything into one .exe
Click to expand...
It's not a good idea to do that with MV to begin with.
For one, exe's simply are meant to execute the launch function of the program and therefore contain very little data. When an exe contains a lot of data, Windows will often false flag them as viruses since it doesn't expect an exe to be large.
Secondly, this can cause read/write issues as well and may result in the game not functioning correctly, incorrectly saving the game, or break how plugins or other aspects of the engine are intended to function.
I cannot speak for Ace, but considering the flaws with packing everything into an exe, I imagine he has no plans to do that since it is ill advised to begin with.
(also, last time I tried Cook Tool Windows still doesn't like the exe's it generates either and still false flags them. lol)

It's been a while since the last release. But today's release (R5.11, codenamed "Kebab") is a quite big release. One of the most notable additions is the support for Quick Loading. Using the included Advanced Save Handler plugin, this allows the game to load the latest save and get the player where they were. It's a nice player facing quality of life improvement, since the player can jump in immediately. In addition, there are quite a lot of technical improvements under the hood, bringing better performance, stability, and a bit of smaller space requirements. Finally, to streamline the setup for Steam Proton compatible builds, the option to create these builds is turned on by default for new projects (alongside the "Protect JavaScript Source Code" option, as the compatibility issues are extremely specific).
Changelog:
Spoiler
Added support for Quick Load (requires the included Advanced Save Handler plugin).
This allows the game to load the latest save file and start the game.
Supports RPG Maker MZ’s Autosave slot.
The feature is accessible on the Bootstrap by passing the --qload command line argument.
Added a “Player friendly version text” to the customization tab.
This is intended for an upcoming feature. If you have a custom launcher made by me, it will use it to show the game’s version better.
Updated dependencies for better performance and stability.
Slight to moderate reduction is space usage.
Slight visual update to the tool and assistant.
Slight update to the bootstrapper’s design.
If an image is in the game files, it will function as a splash screen displayed until the game starts.
Starting with this release, the following changes to the default settings will be applied:
The option "Create Proton compatible builds" (used to create Steam Proton compatible builds) is enabled.
The “Protect JavaScript Source Code” is turned on.
Technical improvements for downloading the required files.
Updates for Advanced Save Handler:
Support for the XDG variables (used on Linux systems to establish standard folders).
Support for XDG folders will be added to the bootstrapper in a future release.
[RPG Maker MV] Added the option to use Brotli compression for saves.
Fixed the following bugs:
[Bootstrapper] An error occurs if automatic removal of game files upon closing is disabled due to task misfires.
The absolute path was set, if you pressed “Browse” and selected the file on the Metadata Editor.

posts.body:
After months of work, a major update to Cook Tool has arrived. While not as extensive as the R5 update, this brings a major overhaul on the tool and the introduction of a new feature. Let’s take a closer look at the release.
Spoiler
Overhauled Game Preparation Pipeline​
The major overhaul in question is Asset Preparation. Combining Asset Compression, JavaScript Source Code protection and the all-new Deep Level Encryption, the asset preparation streamlines the build process, while providing a robust encryption to both RPG Maker MV and MZ. This improves the user experience immensely, as it provides one click to compress, encrypt and protect the game’s assets and code. Simply point it to the source folder and you are good to go. And thanks to the caching system, it takes even less time to prep your game for uploading. Speaking of encryption:
Deep Level Encryption​
Complimenting Halva Package System (if you wish), the all-new Deep Level Encryption is the biggest upgrade for this release. Built on modern web encryption API, DLE brings a robust encryption for the individual assets (images and audio for now). Simply provide a password and the tool will take care of the details. Not only is it fully compatible with existing versions of RPG Maker MV and MZ that support encryption, but it also utilizes NW.js’ JavaScript Source Code Protection, to ensure near perfect protection.
Technical Upgrades​
Finally, a lot of technical updates improve the stability and performance of the tool. From the upgrade to .NET 10, to the overhauled recipe file, R6 polishes up the tool while also building the foundation for future releases.
When will it be released?​
Depending on what’s necessary to fix or implement and when there’s a go-live release of .NET 10, the estimated release date is around August-November of 2025.
Changelog​
Spoiler
Added Deep Level Encryption.
Provides a robust encryption for individual assets.
Merged Asset Compressor, JS Source Code Protection and DLE into “Asset Preparation”.
Merged Halva Settings and Player Services into “Packaging and Player Services”.
Implemented a caching system, speeding up subsequent builds
Overhauled the recipe file spec, allowing better extensibility.
Updated to .NET 10, bringing performance and reliability improvements.
Font Compressor is removed.
I am planning to spin this off into a standalone version of Asset Compressor.
Important Information​
Spoiler
As the preview text implies, this build is not production ready. Early tests do suggest that it’s stable, but it’s not recommended for use with released builds. It’s fine for use with beta builds.
No Linux builds for now. They'll be available at a later preview.
Currently, Version 2 of Recipe files aren’t supported. Automatic migration is coming on the next preview.
Due to the re-work on the build job, the tool might not work correctly with games that were deployed via the editor. This will be addressed in a later preview.
As noted on Deep Level Encryption, source code protection is turned on alongside it. This is a technical necessity, to ensure that the password is protected. Please do test runs with Source Code Protection turned on before using this feature and use the option to create debug builds if the screen is black.

It’s finally here! The biggest update to RPG Maker Cook Tool Deluxe has arrived! A lot of quality-of-life updates, technical improvements and bug fixes have been added to the release, alongside the introduction of the all-new Deep Level Encryption. Let’s take a closer look.
What's new?
Spoiler
Overhauled Asset Pipeline​
As part of a major overhaul, the Asset Compressor, Deep Level Encryption and Source Code Protection has been merged into the Asset Preparation. The new pipeline streamlines the build process, while providing robust encryption for both RPG Maker MV and MZ. This improves the user experience immensely, as it provides a one-click process to compress, encrypt and protect the game’s assets and code. Simply point to the project folder and it will do the rest. And thanks to the new caching system, subsequent builds will be even faster. Plus, it’s highly customizable.
Deep Level Encryption​
Complimenting the Halva Packaging System (if you use it), Deep Level Encryption is the biggest addition to the tool. Built on modern web encryption, it provides a robust encryption to the game’s assets (images and audio for now). Simply give it a password and it will take care of the rest. Not only is it fully compatible with existing versions of RPG Maker MV and MZ that support encryption, but it also utilizes NW.js’ JavaScript Source Code Protection, to ensure near perfect protection.
Quality of Life Improvements​
Finally, a lot of under the hood changes, mixed with merged tools, re-works and minor overhauls went in, to improve the user experience. Tidying up the settings, the overhauled recipe spec, and various tweaks provide a more streamlined, better experience to both you and the players.
Changelog​
Spoiler
Added Deep Level Encryption.
Provides a robust encryption for individual assets (images and audio for now).
Deep Level Encryption is skipped, if there are assets already encrypted via the editor.
Note that if this option is on and no encrypted files are detected, JavaScript Source Code Protection will be turned on as well. This is a necessity to ensure that the password is well protected.
[RPG Maker MV only] You can specify which images to skip for encryption.
[Bootstrap] When you switch DLE on or off between builds, the cache will be rebuilt. This only applies if you turn off the option to clear the cache when the game closes.
Merged Asset Compressor, JS Source Code Protection and DLE into “Asset Preparation”.
Merged Halva Settings and Player Services into “Packaging and Player Services”.
Implemented a caching system, speeding up subsequent builds.
The build cache will also update the relevant files, if the compression and/or the encryption settings are changed.
Overhauled the recipe file spec, allowing better extensibility.
The tool will migrate the old defaults to the new spec automatically.
For the existing recipe files, a filter was added to the file picker that makes it easier to select them. Once opened, migration is done automatically, saving the migrated file on the same place as the original.
[Bootstrap, Windows] The non-Proton compatible build is now built with Windows SDK 10.0.26100.0, improving compatibility.
Lowest version that the game can run on is Windows 10, version 1903.
[Bootstrap] Slight visual tweaks when a splash image is present.
[Linux] Improved decompression performance when decompressing the tar file for the NW.js binaries.
Added a utility to retrieve the logs for the tool.
Tweaked some of the logic that determines if the output folder is the same as (or related to) the source folder.
Tweaked the logic that gets the temporary location for the work folder (when the output folder is not set).
Streamlined some of the checks for certain strings.
Minor performance and memory usage improvements for both the tool and the bootstrap.
Note that due to these changes, the bootstrap manifest and the file catalog generated from this version aren't compatible with older versions.
Re-worked the path construction logic used when creating the Halva packages.
This fixes an issue in Linux, where paths were malformed. That would cause an error due to a non-existent path.
Font Compressor is removed.
I am planning to spin this off into a standalone version of Asset Compressor.
The Migration and Diagnostics Assistant is no longer available, as all functionality is now integrated to the tool.

A minor thing of note: due to changes with Halva’s code (there were changes in the framework that required code changes) the Halva packages may change a bit, resulting in big patches. This is normal, and the patches will return back to normal on subsequent builds.
Changelog:
Spoiler
Improvements to creating test builds:
The checkbox for it was reworked into a drop down (visible in the main window.
The tool will now remove or add the --disable-devtools, depending on the setting.
Added code to certain areas, so it’s easier to see which plug-in broke.

posts.author: AceOfAces
posts.body:
I've released R6.04 today! This release (codenamed "Mousakas") brings quality of life improvements alongside bug fixes. The most notable improvements are the option to build a new version and an overhauled way to handle the output folder. The "Build new version" button (available on the sub-menu near the build button) allows you to punch in the new version and (if you use Halva) the package versions. The package versions are derived from the UTC time, formatted as "yyyyMMddHHmmss". The bootstrapper was updated to handle larger numbers as well (they were originally integers).
The overhauled handling of output folder is to address an issue I was noticing via feedback: before this update, the output folder was treated as a scratch folder. It was expecting that the folder would just hold the builds. However, this had the side effect of deleting other files as well, if the user configured the output to be on a folder that had personal files (and not setting a sub-folder in it). So, if they set it to (for example) C:\Users\<user>\Documents\ but not C:\Users\<user>\Documents\builds, it would delete the Documents folder. To avoid this, I reworked it, so it automatically creates this, in this format:
<output folder>\<developer name>\<product name>\<runtime id>\
Steam builds also work like that:
<output folder>\<developer name>\<product name>\<runtime id>\
To keep a consistency with that format, the output (when the user hasn't set the folder) also reflects this:
Standard build: <project folder>\out\<runtime-id>
Steam build: <project folder>\out\steam-<runtime-id>
I was debating if I should remove that option entirely, since it was an unintentional first user trap. But considering about the features I want to implement and with the new UI in the works, I decided to re-work this.
Sidenote: I'm including changes that were in R6.03u4 - R6.03u6 in the changelog as well.
Changelog​
Spoiler
Added the option to build a new version (accessible in the sub-menu, near the Build button).
Makes it easy to create a new version.
Provides a quick way to also update the package versions as well (if you use Halva compression).
Package versions generated by this, are numbers that are derived from UTC time, formatted as yyyyMMddHHmmss.
Updated the bootstrapper, so it handles large numbers.
Re-worked how the output folder is set.
If an output folder is set in the project settings, it will derive the developer's name and product name to create the actual path, alongside the runtime ID of the tool.
If it's not set, it will set it as <project folder>\out\<runtime id>
Steam builds follow a similar logic for their output.
Updated dependencies, for better performance and stability.
Restructured the settings window, moving the customization options to more logical areas.
Splash screen and bootstrapper settings are now under Halva settings.
Company name, Product Name, Game Version, File Version, Copyright and User-Friendly Version are now under "Essentials".
Moved most of the settings for asset preparation into the "Advanced" section.
Settings related to executable settings and creating the required files for itch.io and Steam are under "Packaging and User Services.
Copyright Info now has formatting support. {0} adds the year. {1} adds the company name.
[Bootstrapper] Fixed a bug, where the manifest carried a path that the Linux version couldn't read.
[RPG Maker MZ] The tool will automatically update the package.json file.
This is a necessity, as the editor also edits the JSON file.
[R6.03u4] Addresses a bug with the save mechanism. Due to an error, the tool wouldn’t overwrite the recipe file properly sometimes.
[R6.03u5] Updated dependencies, bringing stability and performance improvements.
[R6.03u5] The check for when it’s packaged in a MSIX package was reworked so it’s more reliable.
[R6.03u6] Fixed a bug that prevented the tool and bootstrapper from working on Windows 10 systems.
